title: Measuring What the Supplement Overpaid on a Crossover Line
content:
The overpayment on the crossover lines of a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is measured according to why the payment was wrong.

| What the lines show | What is taken as overpaid |
|---|---|
| The lines fall on days this policy did not cover | The whole of what the supplement paid on every line outside cover, none of it having been owed |
| The lines fall on days the policy covered but carry a share the plan letter does not support | Only the part of those payments above the share the plan letter supports on the amounts Medicare approved |
| Neither of those describes them | Nothing is found overpaid |

### The two measures contrasted

Where the days were not covered at all, nothing the supplement paid on those lines was owed, and the whole of it is overpaid.

Where the days were covered, the payment was owed in part: what the plan letter supports is the share it covers taken on the amounts Medicare approved, and only the excess of what was actually paid over that supported figure is overpaid. Where what was paid does not exceed what the plan letter supports, no part of it is overpaid.

### Hypothetical figures

The supplement paid 96.00 and 84.00 on two lines whose dates of service fall on days this policy did not cover: the whole 180.00 is overpaid.

The supplement paid 260.00 on lines falling on covered days, where the amounts Medicare approved come to 240.00 and the share the plan letter covers is 100 per cent, supporting 240.00: the part above that, being 20.00, is overpaid.

The supplement paid 240.00 on covered days where the plan letter supports 240.00: nothing is found overpaid.
